newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss govt still hoping for EU transport deal.
newsitem.headline: Swiss govt still hoping for EU transport deal.

text.p: The Swiss government said on Wednesday it regretted the latest problems in talks to hammer out a bilateral agreement with the European Union (EU) which faltered last week on differences over truck traffic.
In a statement published after a Swiss cabinet meeting, the government said that it was still seeking a deal.

"(The cabinet) has determined that the conclusion of the negotiations have been delayed, namely on the matter of road traffic. The Cabinet regrets this, but it is its intention to continue the negotiations. It assumes that there is also still the will within the EU to reach balanced agreements which are acceptable for both sides," the statement said.
Problems in reaching an agreement forced cancellation of a meeting of European Union transport ministers planned for May 29, when it was hoped a deal might have been reached.

The statement Wednesday also said there would be a meeting Wednesday between Swiss coordinator of the bilateral negotiations Jakob Kellenberger and the EU coordinator Francois Lamoureux. It said this meeting would provide an opportunity to assess the current situation and lead the way ahead.
